activities.caption: call the entropy — English in bits
activities.name: clShannonEstimate

config.prompt: The letter-guessing experiments pegged English's true entropy at roughly how many bits per character?
config.why: About one bit per character of true entropy — the redundancy carries the rest, which is what makes compression, the n-gram baseline and every perplexity story possible.
config.context: Every subsequent breakthrough is partly a lowered-surprise story: statistical MT, embeddings, attention.

activities.caption: pair each corpus finding with what it revealed
activities.name: clLexisMatch

config.prompt: What corpora taught linguistics — pair the finding with its fallout:

pairs.right: words co-occur in semi-fixed patterns far more than generative rules predicted
lexicography pushed from introspection to data — built straight from corpus evidence
exposed which words gravitate to which — meaning structure in numbers
reading difficulty tracks the model's surprise — the language model as a cognitive hypothesis

config.why: The same move reached literature: distant reading (Moretti) treats the corpus as the new archive.

activities.anchor: Between corpora and models sits a quieter infrastructure
activities.caption: file each hand-built resource by what it organises
activities.name: clResourceBuckets

config.prompt: Built largely by hand — file each knowledge resource by the layer it labels:

items.label: WordNet (Princeton, from 1985) — synonym sets linked by hyponymy, meronymy and antonymy
the treebanks of the Penn Treebank — parses over running text
well over 100,000 English words organised into synonym sets

config.why: They powered the rule era's semantics, supervised the statistical era's word-sense disambiguation, and survive into the LLM era as evaluation gold standards — usable under every acquisition story.

activities.caption: find the line the neutrality myth would love
activities.name: clCorpusSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary is the neutrality assumption speaking — click it:
lines: Corpus linguistics made language countable — the founding scaling law fell out of the counts.
A corpus is a neutral window: it records every register equally.
Written language is over-represented relative to spoken.
Synthetic, model-generated text now feeds back into training sets.
config.correction: Corpora are selections with biases — written over spoken, formal over casual, English-dominant, increasingly model-generated.
config.why: Every corpus finding is a finding about that selection; data documentation became a subfield precisely because the neutrality assumption broke.

activities.anchor: Automatic speech recognition shows the whole arc in one task
activities.caption: line up the speech arc, era by era
activities.name: clAsrOrder

config.prompt: One task, the field's whole history — order the arc:
items: Hidden Markov Models treat speech as a statistical sequence problem (1970s–80s)
Usable dictation by the 1990s — word error rates around 25–30% on conversational telephone speech
End-to-end neural models (2015 onward) cross the roughly 5% band that approximates human transcription on benchmarks
The residue: acoustic models carry phones, coarticulation and prosody implicitly — learned rather than hand-specified
config.why: Speech is one of the cleanest cases where the machine rediscovers the linguist's categories from data — and synthesis travelled the same road, from concatenated samples to neural voices indistinguishable in short clips.

activities.caption: drag the divider — benchmark versus deployment
activities.name: clBenchmarkCompare

config.prompt: One claim, two conditions — drag the divider:

before.label: On the benchmark
before.text: End-to-end neural models crossed the roughly 5% error band that approximates human transcription — 'speech recognition is a solved problem.'

after.label: In deployment
after.text: Stanford's 2020 audit of five major commercial systems: average word error rates of about 35% for Black speakers against 19% for white speakers — nearly double — with underrepresentation in training data the likely driver.

config.why: 'Solved' is a claim about test conditions; deployed systems serve populations the benchmark never sampled, so error-rate equity rather than headline accuracy is becoming the honest metric.
